SBhV II 6.13-22: yat khalu tāta kumāra jānīyās, tvaṃ hi sukumāraḥ sukhaiṣī; na tvaṃ jñātā duḥkhasya; duścaraṃ brahmacaryam; duṣkaraṃ prāvivekyaṃ, durabhiramam ekatve, durabhisaṃbudhāny araṇyavanaprasthāni, prāntāni śayanāsanāny adhyāvastum, duḥkham ekākino 'raṇye vāsaḥ; yāvajjīvaṃ te vyāḍamṛgaiḥ saha vastavyam; yāvajjīvaṃ te paradattabhojino bhavitavyam; yāvajjīvaṃ te mānuṣakebhyaḥ kāmebhyaḥ āvaraṇaṃ kartavyam; yāvajjīvaṃ te mānuṣikābhyo ratikrīḍābhya āvaraṇaṃ kartavyam; ehi tvaṃ tāta kumāra ihaiva sthito yauvarājyaṃ kāraya; kāmāṃś ca paribhuṅkṣva; dānāni ca ⟨dehi; puṇyāni ca⟩ kuru
children.translated_text: [Editorial note: <s>Matsumura</s> reads: ekatva(m abhiramaṃ durabhi)sa(ṃ)b(o)dhāny; cf. SBhV II 6.13-22: 'You should know, dear prince, that you are delicate and pleasure-seeking; you do not know suffering; the holy life is hard to practice; seclusion is hard to accomplish; solitude is hard to delight in; forest wilderness retreats and remote dwelling places are hard to inhabit; dwelling alone in the forest is painful; for your whole life you would have to live among wild beasts; for your whole life you would have to subsist on food given by others; for your whole life you would have to abstain from human pleasures; for your whole life you would have to abstain from human sports and amusements. Come, dear prince, remaining right here, exercise the office of crown prince; enjoy pleasures; give gifts; and perform meritorious deeds.']

children.text: sā purāṇajīrṇadāsī śīghraṃśīghraṃ yenāyuṣmato rāṣṭrapālasya mahallakas tenopasaṃkrāntā. upetyāyuṣmato
children.translated_text: Then that old worn-out maidservant very quickly approached the venerable <s>Rāṣṭrapāla's</s> elderly father. Having approached, to the venerable

children.text: svāmi jānīyāḥ, saumyo rāṣṭrapālaḥ sthūlakoṣṭhakaṃ ciraprāptaḥ, svaniveśanaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Master, you should know: dear <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> has arrived at <s>Sthūlakoṣṭhaka</s> some time ago, but to his own residence
[Editorial note: <s>Matsumura</s> reads: 'elderly father' (Tibetan: 'to the father'); manuscript reads mahalla⟨⟨ka⟩⟩m]
he does not wish to come.'

children.text: apālasya mahallako vāmahastena keśaṃ saṃnipātayan paṭakam ekanivāsaṃ nivāsayya yenāyuṣmān rāṣṭrapālo tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>pāla's</s> elderly father, gathering his hair with his left hand and putting on a single cloth garment, approached the venerable <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>.

children.text: ṣmān rāṣṭrapālaḥ prakārakaṇṭake sthitas taṃ paryuṣitaṃ pūtikulmāṣaṃ paribhuñjati.
children.translated_text: able <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> was standing by a wall-buttress, eating that leftover rotten bean porridge.

children.translated_text: cast them there, lest there be for you from this

children.translated_text: [Editorial note: <s>Matsumura</s> reads: 'Having loaded onto carts, in the river... lest there arise for you from this occasion for grief, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair.']
I am unable to make the venerable <s>Rāṣ</s>
[Editorial note: <s>Matsumura</s> reads: 'unable to make dear <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> turn back']
Then the venerable <s>Rāṣṭrapāla's</s> elderly mother, while urging the daughters-in-law, said
'Daughters-in-law! Adorned as you were formerly, having bathed with a bath,
decorated with ornaments, perfumed with incense, with hair-garlands'
the former wives of <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, when he was a householder,

children.text: nāpāś ca tadrūpaiḥ snātraiḥ snātāḥ vastraiḥ prāvṛtāḥ alaṃkāreṇā
children.translated_text: pleasing; bathed with such baths, clothed in garments, adorned with
ornaments, perfumed with incense, with powders
sprinkled, one falling at one foot,

children.text: yā dvitīye nipatitvā evaṃ vadata / kathaṃrūpās tā aps
children.translated_text: falling at the second foot, spoke thus: 'What kind of <s>apsaras</s> (celestial nymphs) are they
for whose sake the noble son, before the <s>Bhagavān</s>,
wife, bathed with such baths, as before
he was a householder, were dear and

children.text: bhū⟨va⟩n manāpāś ca tadrūpaiḥ snānaiḥ snātāḥ pūrvavad yāvac cūrṇair ava
children.translated_text: pleasing; bathed with such baths, as before, and sprinkled with powders, one falling at one

children.text: ūpās tā apsaraso yāsām arthe āryaputro bhaga
children.translated_text: of <s>apsaras</s> (celestial nymphs) are they for whose sake the noble son, before the <s>Bhagavān</s>,

children.text: Matsumura; rāṣṭrap(āla)sya / ⟨pūrve⟩ ā(gāri)kasy(a) ... dvit(ī)yā dvitīye ev(aṃ kathaṃr)ūpās
children.translated_text: [Matsumura's restoration: <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>'s former wife... second at the second... 'What kind of <s>apsaras</s>']
'I do not, sisters, for the sake of <s>apsaras</s> (celestial nymphs)
practice the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) before the <s>Bhagavān</s>.'
Then the venerable <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> addressed his parents: 'Mother,

children.text: parityaktaṃ kiṃ na dīyate kiṃ viheṭhīyat
children.translated_text: has been abandoned, why is it not given away? Why is it being

children.text: Matsumura: aṃ(ba tāta saced annaṃ) parityaktaṃ kiṃ na dīyate kiṃ viheṭhīyat(e parityakte)
children.translated_text: [Matsumura's restoration: 'Mother, Father, if food has been abandoned, why is it not given away? Why is it wasted, when abandoned?']
parents, having risen from their seats,
and excellent hard and soft food with their own hands, satisfying and nourishing him.

children.text: aṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ santarpayanti saṃpravārayanti. anekaparyāyeṇa śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ santarpayitvā saṃpravārayitvā
children.translated_text: and excellent hard and soft food with their own hands, satisfying and nourishing him. Having in various ways with pure and excellent hard and soft food satisfied and nourished him with their own hands,

children.text: āyuṣmantaṃ rāṣṭrapālaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastam apanītapātraṃ nīcatarakam āsanaṃ gṛhītvā niṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya
children.translated_text: knowing that the venerable <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> had eaten, had washed his hands, and had put aside his bowl, they took a lower seat and sat down for the hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: athāyuṣmān rāṣṭrapālas tasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthā babhāṣe.
children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, at that time, spoke these verses:
...... having renounced sensual pleasures, the monastic life (<s>śrāmaṇya</s>)
the great king <s>Kauravya</s>, [having heard] the venerable <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>'s
bowed at the feet of the venerable one
head, rose from his seat, and departed.
